Environment names and values use repeated form fields, preserving list order. Supply one value for every name, with equal counts and matching positions; this cross-parameter condition is documented but is not enforced by a new client validator. Lists use the shared nonempty sequential string-list boundary; values are sensitive. Omitted options retain server defaults, while explicit false is sent as 0 and strings such as "0" remain strings.

The response is keyed by application name. Each application retains its optional declared fields; envvars is an opaque object whose values have no pinned type. Its unknown variable names and nested values are preserved. enabled in these mutation responses remains an integer 0/1 flag.

Supplying environment variables replaces all existing variables. clear_envvars defaults to 0 and asks whether to clear variables; the source does not define precedence when combined with replacement variables. Omitted deployment_mode, domain, new_name and path keep their current values; enabled has the documented default 1. Paths are sent unchanged. For a WebApp application use WebApp::configure.

evidence.note: The pinned /PassengerApps/edit_application operation declares x-readonly=false and x-rollback=none; use form POST for mutations and keep supplied environment values out of query strings.

Pinned envvar_name and envvar_value are arrays of strings with paired multi-value examples. Registration declares style=form and explode=true for both. Edit declares style=form and explode=true for names; values use style=form with explode omitted, whose OpenAPI default is true. These declarations support repeated envvar_name and envvar_value fields, not comma serialization or indexed parameter names.

Starts asynchronous dependency installation for gem (Gemfile), npm (package.json) or pip (requirements.txt). API success confirms the start request, not completion. Optional task_id and sse_url remain response payload; the client does not follow the SSE URL or poll. WebApp::deploy installs dependencies as part of deployment.

Returns a map keyed by application name, including an empty map when no applications are present. Declared row fields remain optional. enabled has no pinned schema, so it remains mixed rather than inheriting an integer flag constraint from mutation responses. envvars is an optional nullable opaque object; unknown environment names and values remain intact.

deps contains optional gem, npm and pip command strings; the documented no-dependency value is the string "0", not integer zero. nodejs, python and ruby appear only for the configured runtimes. Returned commands and paths are data and are not executed or followed. For a WebApp application use WebApp::list.

Only registers an already-created application; it does not create application files. The path prose says relative to the account home, while its example begins with a slash; the client forwards the supplied path unchanged. base_uri defaults to /, deployment_mode to production, and enabled to 1 when omitted. For new WebApp applications use WebApp::stage and WebApp::deploy.

Environment names may contain letters, numbers, underscores and dashes, may not begin with a number and must not exceed 256 characters. Values must contain at most 1024 ASCII-printable characters. These source restrictions are documented; the shared repeated-field encoder does not invent additional per-character validation.
